verdict.rationale: cubic supports org-wide defaults: you create a `cubic-config` repository in the organization with a root `cubic.yaml` (cubic-docs-67), and custom agents enforce organization-specific rules across pull requests (cubic-docs-9). Per-repo `cubic.yaml` files act as the source of truth for review behavior (cubic-docs-11), which implies repo-level exceptions, but those are managed in each repo rather than centrally. RBAC governs who can change settings (cubic-docs-56). missing for 10: documented inheritance/override precedence between the org config and repo configs, central management of per-repo exceptions, evidence of rollout at hundreds-of-repos scale, independent corroboration.
